title: H600 Weather Station | Configurable Weather Monitoring | Hitelecom
metaDescription: Configure the Hitelecom H600 weather station with 2–12 sensor channels, solar or mains power, selected wireless connectivity and online monitoring in Hitelecom Cloud.
imageAlt: Hitelecom H600 weather-station terminal enclosure with branded front panel and mounting support, official product image
caption: H600 · Weather-station terminal shown
heroValue:
Local weather.
Connected to your site.
heroDescription: The Hitelecom H600 brings selected meteorological measurements into a connected site-monitoring system. Configure 2–12 sensor channels around the weather information your team needs, with solar or mains power and a selected 4G LTE, NB-IoT or LoRa version. View uploaded monitoring data online in Hitelecom Cloud and receive alerts when readings exceed configured thresholds, or agree integration with a compatible customer platform.

featureTitle:
Weather measurements.
Defined around the site.
featureIntro: Specify the measurements, power and data path as one station configuration. Keep sensor performance, reporting requirements and installation conditions visible from selection through handover.

features.title: Configurable measurement channels
features.text: Select 2–12 sensor channels for the project. Meteorological options include air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and direction, atmospheric pressure, rainfall and solar radiation; the supplied channel schedule defines the actual set.

features.title: Solar or mains power
features.text: Choose a solar-power or mains-power configuration around sensor demand, the sampling and reporting profile, site exposure and available infrastructure. Confirm the supplied power assembly and maintenance requirements.

features.title: Selected wireless connectivity
features.text: Specify the 4G LTE, NB-IoT or LoRa version for the deployment. Match cellular hardware to the local operator; a LoRa installation requires the agreed compatible receiving path and platform integration.

features.title: Online data and threshold alerts
features.text: Use Hitelecom Cloud to view uploaded monitoring data online and receive alerts when measurements exceed configured thresholds. Define the monitored points, limits and notification recipients around the site workflow.

features.title: MQTT platform integration
features.text: Bring the selected records into Hitelecom Cloud or a compatible customer platform. Agree the data path, endpoint, message format, device identity, measurement units and authentication configuration.

features.title: IP65 installation reference
features.text: The published station protection reference is IP65. Specify enclosure sealing, cable entries, sensor exposure and mounting as a complete installation; confirm the ratings and operating limits of the supplied components.

features.title: NFC-enabled local setup
features.text: NFC-enabled configurations support activation and local device setup. Confirm the supplied hardware, available configuration functions and commissioning procedure for the project.

features.title: Remote firmware maintenance
features.text: Supported configurations provide OTA firmware updates through the agreed remote-management path. Confirm firmware compatibility, connectivity and the update procedure during commissioning.

planningIntro: A useful weather record begins with the measurement objective and exposure at the sensing point. Plan the channel schedule, station locations, power and onward connection together.

planning.title: Define the measurements
planning.text: List the required quantities and distinguish measured channels from any calculations expected in a receiving system. Specify the sensor range, accuracy, resolution, units, sampling interval and reporting interval for each selected channel.
planning.brief: Channel schedule · Sensor ranges and accuracy · Sampling · Reporting · Required alerts

planning.title: Plan the observation points
planning.text: Assess terrain, surrounding structures, vegetation, nearby heat sources and exposure. Select sensor positions and mounting arrangements that suit the measurement objective, with access for inspection and cleaning.
planning.brief: Site layout · Sensor exposure · Mounting position · Maintenance access · Representative conditions

planning.title: Size power and the data path
planning.text: Review sensor loads, the reporting profile, available sunlight or mains supply and the selected communications version. Confirm the receiving system and verify the end-to-end data path with the supplied configuration.
planning.brief: Power budget · Solar or mains supply · Operator or LoRa receiving path · MQTT mapping · Acceptance checks

installationText: Plan the mast or support, foundation or mounting interface, sensor exposure, cable routing and service access as one installation. Account for shading, structures, turbulence and local heat sources that could affect the measurements. Solar supply and wireless reporting still require a suitable power budget, an available data path and a maintained sensing assembly.

workflow.title: Measure the selected channels
workflow.text: The configured sensors measure the specified weather quantities. Record the channel identity, units and relevant sensor performance conditions in the project schedule.

workflow.title: Report through the selected version
workflow.text: Send records according to the agreed sampling and reporting profile through the supplied 4G LTE, NB-IoT or LoRa configuration and its compatible onward data path.

workflow.title: View data and respond
workflow.text: View uploaded monitoring data online in Hitelecom Cloud and receive alerts when readings exceed configured thresholds. A customer platform can provide its own agreed displays, notification workflow and data handling.

faqs.q: Which weather parameters can the H600 measure?
faqs.a: The H600 is configured with 2–12 selected sensor channels. Meteorological options include air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and direction, atmospheric pressure, rainfall and solar radiation. The actual sensor set is defined for the project. Product images identify the terminal; supplied sensors and mounting follow the project configuration.

faqs.q: How many channels should I specify?
faqs.a: The H600 product reference is 2–12 configurable sensor channels. Start with the quantities needed for the project, then select the sensors and record the actual channel set in the supplied configuration. The channel schedule defines what is measured at the site.

faqs.q: What are the measurement range and accuracy?
faqs.a: Range, accuracy and resolution depend on the selected sensor and working conditions. Specify these for every required quantity, including the applicable range, exposure and any calibration documentation. There is no single accuracy figure that describes all H600 channels.

faqs.q: How are sampling, reporting and alerts configured?
faqs.a: Define the sampling interval, reporting interval and threshold-notification requirements separately. Their implementation depends on the selected sensors, communications version, power system and platform configuration. Agree the required operating profile and verify it during commissioning.

faqs.q: Can the station use solar power at a remote site?
faqs.a: A solar-power configuration can be selected for a suitable site. Size the power system for the sensor loads, operating profile and local solar conditions, and provide the required mounting, communication coverage and maintenance access. A fixed autonomy period is not specified for every configuration.

faqs.q: Which communication version should I select?
faqs.a: Choose the 4G LTE, NB-IoT or LoRa version around the site and receiving system. Match cellular bands and modem configuration to the local operator. A LoRa project needs an agreed compatible receiver or gateway and onward integration; LoRa alone does not establish LoRaWAN interoperability.

faqs.q: Can the H600 connect to a customer platform?
faqs.a: A compatible customer-platform integration can be agreed using the published MQTT data approach. Define the complete data path, endpoint, topics, payload mapping, device identity, units, timestamps and supported authentication for the supplied communication version.

faqs.q: What can users do in Hitelecom Cloud?
faqs.a: Users can view uploaded monitoring data online and receive alerts when readings exceed configured thresholds. Agree the channel views, threshold values, notification recipients and operating workflow for the project, and verify them with representative measurements.

faqs.q: Are NFC setup and OTA updates available?
faqs.a: NFC activation and local configuration, and remote OTA firmware updates, are listed in the product reference. Confirm their availability, supported settings and operating procedure for the supplied hardware, firmware and platform configuration.

faqs.q: Does IP65 apply to every part of the installed station?
faqs.a: IP65 is the published station protection reference. The sensing elements, enclosure, connectors, power assembly and mounting must be specified for their individual exposure and installation conditions. Confirm the ratings and operating limits of the complete supplied assembly.

faqs.q: What installation and maintenance planning is needed?
faqs.a: Plan representative sensor exposure, mounting, power, the data path and service access. Nearby structures, vegetation, shading, heat sources and surface conditions can affect observations. Follow the supplied inspection, cleaning and maintenance procedures for the selected sensors and power system.

faqs.q: How does the H600 differ from the H700 hydrology station?
faqs.a: H600 is configured around meteorological observations such as wind, rainfall, atmospheric conditions and solar radiation. H700 is configured around water-level, flow-related, water-quality and associated environmental channels. Select the platform and sensing assemblies by the required monitored quantities.
